title: Nonnegative strictly graded commutative algebras
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A nonnegatively graded unital $R$-algebra [def-sfb-nonnegative-graded-algebra] consists of an associative unital $R$-algebra $A$ and $R$-submodules $A_i$ for $i\geq0$, such that the additive sum map $\bigoplus_{i\geq0}A_i\to A$ is an isomorphism, $1\in A_0$, the image of $R$ lies in $A_0$, and $A_i A_j\subseteq A_{i+j}$. Put $A_i=0$ for $i<0$. An element of $A_i$ is homogeneous of degree $i$. The algebra is strictly graded commutative if $xy=(-1)^{ij}yx$ for every homogeneous $x\in A_i,y\in A_j$ and $x^2=0$ for every homogeneous element of odd degree. Write $A_{\mathrm{even}}=\bigoplus_{i\geq0}A_{2i}$, $A_{\mathrm{odd}}=\bigoplus_{i\geq0}A_{2i+1}$ and $A_{\mathrm{even},+}=\bigoplus_{i>0}A_{2i}$. The even part is a commutative subalgebra and its positive-degree part is an ideal in it.

source.place: Tag 09PF (section-tate), paragraphs immediately preceding Tag 09PG (definition-divided-powers-graded): graded algebras, parity parts and strict graded commutativity.

proof.text: Use the internal direct-sum grading of [def-sfb-nonnegative-graded-algebra]. The displayed parity sums mean their images inside $A$: an element is a finite sum of homogeneous components with respectively even, odd, or strictly positive even indices. These images are $R$-submodules, since addition, negation, and scalar multiplication preserve the indicated indices. The restricted sum maps are injective because the full sum map is injective. Thus these are genuine submodules of the given algebra, without any choice of new data.

source.place: Tag 09PF, section-tate, introductory grading and parity conventions, lines 951–962; Tag 09PG, definition-divided-powers-graded, following observation at lines 985–990.

proof.text: For the final structural assertions, $1$ and the scalar image lie in $A_0\subseteq A_{\mathrm{even}}$ by [def-sfb-nonnegative-graded-algebra]. Multiplication sends $A_{2i}A_{2j}$ into $A_{2(i+j)}$, so finite distributivity proves closure of the even submodule under multiplication. The defining sign rule gives $xy=yx$ on these homogeneous components because $(-1)^{(2i)(2j)}=1$; expanding two finite sums proves commutativity on the whole even part. Hence the inherited operations make it a commutative $R$-subalgebra. If $j>0$, then $i+j>0$ for every $i\geq0$, so the same expansion shows that multiplication by any even element preserves the positive even submodule. This proves it is an ideal of the even subalgebra. Associativity, distributivity, and the unit equations are inherited from $A$.
